A' peace, whats the matter there? By no meanes, nor out of neither of the Fiſhſtreets, admit not a man; they are not Chriſtmas creatures: Fiſh, and faſting dayes, foh! Sonnes, ſayd I well? looke too't. Right Sonne. How now? what's the matter? Why, here is no place for you. Good Lady Venus of Pudding-lane, you muſt go out for all this. No matter for your Pedigree, your houſe; good Venus will you depart? Fie, fie, fie; it's naught, it's naught boyes. No matter, his owne face ſhall ſerve for a puniſhment, and 'tis bad enough; has Waſſell her boule, and Mince-pie her ſpoones? Let him hold his peace, and his diſgrace will bee the leſſe: what? ſhall wee proclaime where wee were furniſht? Mum! Mum! a' peace, be readie good Boyes. Come, you put Robin Cupid out with your waters, and your fiſling; will you be gone? Will you peace, forſooth? Nay, he is out enough, you may take him away, and begin your Dance; this it is to have ſpeeches. Well done Boyes, my fine Boyes, my bully Boyes.
Here's one, o' Friday ſtreet would come in. No bodie out o' Friday-ſtreet, nor the two Fiſh-ſtreets there; doe yo heare? Yes, he may ſlip in for a Torch-bearer, ſo he melt not too faſt, that he will laſt till the Maſque be done. It ſhall not need, heer's your Son Chrater without; has Cards in his pocket. And heer's New-yeares-gift h'as an Orenge, and Roſmarie, but not a clove to ſticke in't.
Shall John Butter o' Milke-ſtreet come in? aske him. Why? here be halfe of the properties forgotten, Father. Ha' you nere a Son at the Groom-Porters to beg, or borrow a paire of Cards quickly? And Mumming, has not his vizard neither.
Now, all the Lords bleſſe me, where am I tro? where is Cupid: ſerve the King? they may ſerve the Cobler well enough, ſome of 'em, for any courteſie they have y'wiſſe; they ha' need o' mending: unrude people they are, your Courtiers, here was thruſt upon thruſt indeed! was it ever ſo hard to get in before, tro? A place forſooth, I do want a place; I would have a good place to ſee my Child act in before the KING, and QUENES Majeſties (God bleſſe 'em) to night. Right forſooth, I am Cupids Mother, Cupids owne Mother: for ſooth; yes forſooth: I dwell in pudding-lane; I forſooth, he is Pren tiſe in Love-lane with a Bugle-maker, that makes of your Bobs, and Bird-bolts for Ladies, Yes forſooth, I can ſit any where, ſo I may ſee Cupid act; hee is a pretty Child, though I ſay it that perhaps ſhould not, you will ſay: I had him by my firſt Husband, he was a Smith forſooth, we dwelt in Doe-little lane then, he came a moneth before his time, and that may make him ſomewhat imperfect: But I was a Fiſhmongers daughter. I forſooth, he'le ſay his part I warrant him, as well as ere a Play boy of 'em all: I could ha' had money enough for him, an I would ha beene tempted, and ha' let him out by the weeke, to the Kings Players: Maſter Burbadge has beene about and about with me; and ſo has old Mr. Hemings too, they ha' need of him, where is he tro'a? I would faine ſee him, pray God they have given him ſome drinke ſince he came. Why, I have cloves, if it be cloves you want, I have cloves in my purſe, I never goe without one in my mouth. Tis a good child, ſpeake out, hold up your head Love. Do not ſhake ſo Robin, if thou beeſt a'cold, I ha' ſome warme waters for thee, here. I forſooth; hee's a child, you muſt conceive, and muſt be uſ'd tenderly; he was never in ſuch an aſſembly before forſooth, but once at Warmoll Queſt, forſooth, where he ſayd grace as prettily as any of the Sheriffes Hinch-boyes forſooth. I that's a good boy, ſpeake plaine, Robin: how does his Ma jeſtie like him, I pray? will he give eight pence a day thinke you? ſpeak out Robin. You wrong the Child, you doe wrong the Infant; I' peale to his Majeſtie.
Are you readie Boyes? ſtrike up, nothing will drown this noiſe but a Drum: a' peace, yet, I ha' not done
Poſt and Paire wants his pur-chops, and his pur-dogs. Odds ſo; ſpeake to the Guard to let him in, under the name of a propertie.
Why, let one go to the Spicery.
I, I; but Miſ-rule doth not like his ſuite: he ſaies the Players have lent him one too little, on purpoſe to diſgrace him.
You worthie wights, King, Lords, and Knights, or Queene, and Ladies bright: Cupid invites, you to the ſights he ſhall preſent to night. And which Cupid —and which Cupid, &c. And which Cupid, and which Cupid, &c.
